correctness.rationale: The fiber law itself is correct, but the Finding falsely calls the valuation-layer targets central. For example, in AGL_1(Z/9Z), conjugating (1,1) by (2,0) gives (1,2), so the valuation-zero translation (1,1) is not central. In general, commutation with all translations forces the multiplier of a central element to be 1, and (1,t) is then central exactly when (a-1)t=0 for all units a. For q>2 a unit difference can be a unit, so only t=0 is central. For q=2 the unit differences form the maximal ideal and the central translations are indexed by its annihilator pi^(n-1)R. The intended layer counts hold for translation targets, not central targets. To check the valid part, subtract the translations of gh and hg (their multipliers agree); the resulting commutator translation is (a-1)y-(b-1)x. For fixed units its image is pi^s R with s=min(v(a-1),v(b-1)), and each nonempty fiber has q^(n+s) elements. There are N_s^2-N_(s+1)^2 pairs at s<n, and only (1,1) as a pair of units at s=n. This proves the formula, the q=2 cutoff, and strict increase on the attained layers. Summing the identity fiber gives |G| times N_0+(q^n-1)/(q-1), in agreement with the examples and class count. Changing 'central targets' to 'translation targets' fixes the false count wording but does not remove the coverage issue.
residual_risks: Replay with python3 checker.py; selected modular and dual-number rings corroborate the formula, not the claim about centrality. The checker compares the identity fiber with a supplied class-number formula, not a separate partition of the group into classes.
The argument does not count fibers for general non-chain rings.

evidence: For r<n the resulting fiber is |G| times [N_0+sum_(m=1)^r q^(n-m)-q^(n-r-1)/(q-1)]; at r=n omit the last negative term. At r=0 this gives q^(3n-1)(q-2). Its successive differences are (q^2-1)q^(3n-r-2) at 1<=r<n and q^(2n) at r=n, exactly q^(n+r) M_r in the frozen formula. The layer sizes are the same differences of chain ideal sizes.

originality.rationale: The valid all-target law is a direct consequence of the full character values in the distinct indexed record Conjugacy and ordinary character spectra of affine groups over finite chain rings. Its detailed table covers the exact same chain-ring assumptions, both mixed and equal characteristic, and includes residue field of order two. The standard Frobenius commutator formula turns the explicit character-to-degree ratios at translations directly into the prescribed fibers. This demonstrates coverage even without a verbatim fiber claim. The two records have the same displayed date; neither precedence nor derivation is inferred.

value.rationale: Nonidentity word-map fibers over chain rings are a natural question, and a direct ideal-filtration proof is a convenient explanation. But the surviving invariant and its valuation and residue-size consequences are mechanically recoverable from the inspected full table by one standard character sum. No further independent mathematical gain is established by the frozen finding; the direct calculation is useful exposition of covered data.
residual_risks: No judgment is made about the value of the stronger character-table classification itself or of a different word map.
